data.name: Josette
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name ‘Yosefet’, meaning 'God will add'. Josette is a French diminutive of Joséphine or Josephine, which is derived from the Hebrew name Joseph. data.cultural_impact: The name Josette gained popularity in France and other French-speaking countries due to the French saint Josette, who lived during the late Middle Aages. Her story of generosity and kindness has inspired many, and the name Josette has become a symbol of these virtues.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Josette holds the meaning 'God will add', implying that God is always adding to our lives in ways that may not be immediately apparent. It is a reminder that even in difficult times, God is working in our lives to bring about something greater. Additionally, the name Josette is associated with the virtues of generosity and kindness, which are essential aspects of the Christian faith and a call to live out our faith in our daily lives.

historical_references.reference: Josette of Bourbon was born in 1477 as the daughter of Jean I, Duke of Bourbon. She married Charles, Duke of Alençon in 1491, and they had five children together. Josette is best known for her involvement in the Italian Wars, supporting her husband's efforts against the French. She died in 1505.
